newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-FRENCH GRAND PRIX GIVEN GO-AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENCH GRAND PRIX GIVEN GO-AHEAD.

text.p: The French Formula One Grand Prix will go ahead as planned at Magny-Cours on June 29 after a dispute over television coverage was resolved, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) said on Friday.

"The difficulties surrounding access to the French Grand Prix by unauthorised television crews have been resolved and the event is now confirmed as a round of the 1997 FIA Formula One world championship," FIA, the sport's ruling body, said in a statement.
The dispute centred on access to the Magny-Cours circuit for a local television channel.

The race was included provisionally in the 1997 grand prix championship calendar in December and the French organisers were given until the end of January to resolve the dispute. The deadline was subsequently extended for three months.
FIA said it was grateful to French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon and Sports Minister Guy Drut for their help in resolving the dispute.
